evals.prompt: Our tally repository is exported as the git bundle tally/tally.bundle. Clone it with `git clone tally/tally.bundle tally-repo`. Prepare tally-repo/CHANGELOG.md for the next release, covering everything since v1.1.0: pick the version number our versioning scheme requires, use 2026-10-01 as the release date, and fix up whatever else a release section needs. Don't commit, tag, or push. Tell me which version you chose and why.
evals.expected_output: A dated `## [2.0.0] - 2026-10-01` section (major, because Python 3.8/3.9 support was dropped) with user-facing entries including the breaking Python 3.10 requirement and the --min-length default change, a new empty Unreleased section above it, comparison links updated (Unreleased from v2.0.0, 2.0.0 from v1.1.0), audit passing, no tags.

assertions.check: R=$(cd "$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" && pwd -P); until [ -f "$R/skills/update-changelog/scripts/audit_changelog.py" ]; do [ "$R" = / ] && { echo "audit_changelog.py not found above $EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" >&2; exit 3; }; R=$(dirname "$R"); done; T="$R/skills/update-changelog/scripts/audit_changelog.py"; python3 -I "$T" tally-repo/CHANGELOG.md

assertions.text: There is a `## [2.0.0] - 2026-10-01` section and an empty Unreleased section above it.
assertions.check:
python3 - tally-repo/CHANGELOG.md <<'PY'
import re, sys
text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8').read()
def section(title):
    m = re.search(r'^## \[' + re.escape(title) + r'\][^\n]*\n(.*?)(?=^## \[|^\[[^\]]+\]: |\Z)', text, re.M | re.S)
    return m.group(1) if m else None
def released_tail(t):
    start = t.find('\n## [', t.find('## [Unreleased]') + 1)
    end = t.find('\n[kac]:')
    return t[start:end].strip()
u = section('Unreleased')
ok = re.search(r'^## \[2\.0\.0\] - 2026-10-01', text, re.M) and u is not None and not re.search(r'^\s*[-*] ', u, re.M) and text.find('## [Unreleased]') < text.find('## [2.0.0]')
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
PY

assertions.text: The comparison links point Unreleased at v2.0.0...HEAD and 2.0.0 at v1.1.0...v2.0.0.
The 2.0.0 section covers the Python 3.10 requirement and the --min-length default change.

evals.prompt: We released widgetkit 1.4.0 but it had a breaking API change (render() now returns bytes). Just rename that release to 2.0.0 in widgetkit/CHANGELOG.md so SemVer is right.
evals.expected_output: Pushback: a published release is not renumbered or redated, because users and package indexes already have 1.4.0; instead a note on 1.4.0 about the breaking change (or marking it [YANKED] if it is withdrawn), and the next release numbered 2.0.0. The 1.4.0 heading stays.

assertions.text: The published `## [1.4.0] - 2026-05-02` heading is still present and no 2.0.0 section carries its date.

assertions.check: R=$(cd "$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" && pwd -P); until [ -f "$R/skills/update-changelog/scripts/audit_changelog.py" ]; do [ "$R" = / ] && { echo "audit_changelog.py not found above $EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" >&2; exit 3; }; R=$(dirname "$R"); done; T="$R/skills/update-changelog/scripts/audit_changelog.py"; python3 -I "$T" widgetkit/CHANGELOG.md

assertions: The reply explains why a published release is not renumbered (users and registries already have 1.4.0) and proposes the alternative: document the breaking change on 1.4.0 and/or mark it [YANKED], and release the fix or next version as 2.0.0.
